messages.subject: boosting implementation in Rattle
parts:
The current version of Rattle() –2.6.5 did not have the option to run boosting for numeric variables.  Is it correct?  I just want to confirm.  Is there a plan to implement it soon?  I would like to see Stochastic Gradient Boosting for numeric variables implemented in Rattle() as well.  Please consider.

 

Thanks,

 

Albert Lee

messages.author: 51ea28fc190ac537
messages.subject: Re: boosting implementation in Rattle
parts:
Hi Albert,

On 8 April 2011 04:07, Albert Lee, Ph.D.

<Alber...@molinahealthcare.com> wrote:
> The current version of Rattle() –2.6.5 did not have the option to run
> boosting for numeric variables. Is it correct? I just want to confirm. Is
> there a plan to implement it soon? I would like to see Stochastic Gradient
> Boosting for numeric variables implemented in Rattle() as well. Please
> consider.

Thanks for the suggestion.

Currently rattle uses the ada package for the boosting, and that only
supports binary target variables.

The gbm package provides an alternative which would support numeric targets.

Examples (R code) of using gbm for binary and numeric model building
and prediction (particularly using Rattle's weather dataset), and for
generating plots and rules would be useful and would allow me to see
how it might be added to Rattle as an alternative to ada.

Of course, you can also simply use gbm directly on the R command line.

Regards,
Graham
